markdown_report:
The best next experiment remains a frozen SASRec with a scale-normalized recent-history residual, selected exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10. At 10% research progress, prioritize this feasible hypothesis test; neither improvement nor functional compatibility is established.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Freezing SASRec isolates the residual’s immediate contribution; zero weight preserves baseline scores. This does not measure encoder adaptation. (2) Recent similarity may strengthen specific interests or amplify substitutes. Preserve repeated events without assuming they imply unmet needs. (3) Margin magnitudes depend on scale. Normalization supports comparison but is not probability calibration or evidence of complementary information.

**Insights from supplied related work.** (1) The [recency study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) motivates testing excessive recent-item emphasis; no optimal horizon follows for these categories. (2) [Sampled-metric analysis](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) establishes possible ranking reversals; simulator feedback supplements the pinned objective. (3) The [complementary-reranking paper](https://genai-personalization.github.io/assets/papers/GenAIRecP2025/5_Xu.pdf) distinguishes functional relationships from similarity; titles cannot verify compatibility or needs. (4) [Selection-bias analysis](https://jmlr.org/papers/volume11/cawley10a/cawley10a.pdf) motivates reporting every configuration; selecting a validation winner creates optimism.

Three directions follow: normalize recency, diagnose sensitivity, and audit relationship evidence.

| Direction | Existing signal | Proposed extension | Unresolved gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recency | SASRec contextual scores | Frozen cosine residual | Useful horizon varies |
| Sensitivity | Training-pair margins | Residual-off paired comparisons | Generalization remains unproven |
| Relationships | Titles/descriptions | Evidence-backed overlap flags | Actual needs are unobserved |

Three candidate ideas remain; difficulty increases with score. Each assessment includes a positive and negative reason.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Normalized recent residual | 3: controlled combination; familiar components | 6: cheap hypothesis test; shared embeddings may be redundant | 3: scoring-only addition; export and causal checks required |
| History-coherence gate | 5: adaptive residual; heuristic gate | 6: history-dependent recency; coherence may misrepresent intent | 4: simple statistics; additional tuning |
| Text-supported overlap penalty | 5: evidence-grounded reranking; established approach | 6: addresses overlap; repetition can be desirable | 6: no pretrained weights needed; brittle lexical rules |

**Selected algorithm.** Normalize frozen item embeddings; normalize the mean of the latest K nonpadding events through each input position, excluding its next-item target. Add α times cosine similarity scaled by the training-pair margin standard-deviation ratio, with denominator floor and cap. This heuristic equalizes margin variability; correlated signals remain redundant.

Compare baseline against K∈{3,10}, α∈{0.05,0.10,0.20}; prefer baseline on ties. Prespecified controls compare last-item, full-prefix, random-K, oldest-K and training-count popularity residuals. Window-internal shuffling is ineffective for mean pooling. Report all configurations, checkpoint selection, category gains/losses and paired macro differences; winner-only bootstrap intervals are not selection-adjusted.

Preserve four routes, seeds, splits, DATA_DIR and predictor serialization. Expose residual-off scoring to DiagnosisProbe; verify exported-score agreement, padding, repeats and future-token invariance. Training diagnostics and twenty-user feedback remain descriptive; cosine normalization does not exclude popularity shortcuts.

idea.description: Freeze each category’s SASRec and add a candidate-independent, scale-normalized cosine residual from its most recent K interaction events. Include the unchanged baseline in validation selection. Retain the original experiment and add prespecified controls for recency, popularity, repeated events, numerical stability and export consistency.
idea.motivation: The diagnosis suggests that broad relevance sometimes overwhelms recent specific interests. A small residual tests whether emphasizing those interests improves the fixed benchmark, while acknowledging that similarity can amplify substitutes and cannot establish compatibility, fulfilled needs or current purchase intent. Shared SASRec embeddings may make the added signal redundant. At 10% research progress, this controlled experiment remains preferable to introducing a coherence gate or brittle text-based penalties before establishing incremental value.
idea.implementation_notes:
Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four category routes, original input splits, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Train the baseline once per category within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget, recording its existing checkpoint-selection rule and every inspected validation result. Freeze parameters and use evaluation mode. No test labels, hidden files, external data, pretrained weights or evaluator changes are permitted.

Use one shared K and alpha configuration across categories, selected by pinned macro validation HR@10; break ties in favor of alpha=0. The primary search remains K={3,10}, alpha={0.05,0.10,0.20}, plus baseline. Prespecify supplementary controls before inspecting their results: last-item, full available causal prefix, uniformly sampled K events without replacement and oldest-K, using the same alpha grid. Use the same sampled event subsets across candidates and alpha values. A training-count popularity control uses log1p(item training count), with its own training-margin scale normalization. Record any additional K=5, robust-scale or unique-item pooling experiment as an expansion of the search scope. Preserve repeated events in the main representation. Event-weighted versus unique-item pooling is an ablation, not a preprocessing change. Shuffling events within the same mean-pooled window cannot test order sensitivity.

Estimate category- and K-specific scales from the first ten batches of a separate nonshuffled loader over the existing causal training examples, using a dedicated generator seeded 42 for any negative draws. Reuse these examples and negatives across residual variants; record their IDs or an equivalent reproducible specification. Exclude positions with padding and nonfinite margins. Compute population standard deviations in float64. Set k=0 when fewer than two valid pairs exist, either standard deviation is nonfinite, or the cosine-margin standard deviation is at most 1e-3; otherwise set k=min(std(base_margin)/std(cosine_margin),100). These fixed numerical safeguards are engineering choices, not validated guarantees. Normalize embeddings and history means with epsilon=1e-8, leaving padding and empty histories zero. Scale normalization is not probability calibration: it ignores margin means and correctness. Record margin correlation because Var(base_margin + alpha*k*cosine_margin)=sigma_base^2*(1+alpha^2+2*alpha*rho) when the ratio is uncapped and nondegenerate. If robust alternatives are explored, specify normalized MAD or IQR and zero-scale fallbacks in advance; they introduce additional configurations.

Save checkpoint, K, alpha, category-specific scale, normalization epsilon, dtype, scale estimator, safeguards, sampling seeds, and event-pooling policy beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct identical scoring and category routing. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model must remain the actual deployed nn.Module. The compatibility view can return concatenated SASRec and recent-history features of shape B×L×2D; predict_score must support that layout and expose predict_score_base. Preserve item_emb, user_train, meta_data and review_data, explicitly marking unavailable fields and simulator traits unavailable. Only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps may support additional analyses; ignore the generic metadata examples containing prohibited fields.

Verify diagnostic and exported scores in evaluation mode on identical prefixes, candidate IDs and frozen weights. Use short left-padded histories, repeated items, empty prefixes where supported, and modified future tokens; earlier-position scores must remain invariant. Check finite values and float32 score agreement with atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-5; compare rankings with explicit handling of numerical ties. A mismatch invalidates the ablation until corrected.

Report baseline and every configuration’s per-category and macro validation HR@10, paired user hit differences, and counts gained/lost. For descriptive uncertainty, perform 10,000 paired bootstrap replicates with seed 42, resampling 200 users within each category and averaging category differences equally. These intervals condition on trained models, fixed candidates and categories; they exclude seed and candidate-draw variation and are not selection-adjusted when applied to the chosen winner. Six prespecified baseline comparisons may receive Holm-adjusted paired tests or simultaneous intervals, but these do not remove winner optimism or cover later adaptive searches. Call validation results exploratory. Training-only chronological inner windows could support a future tuning protocol with cutoff-specific preprocessing and auxiliary retraining, but incur budget costs and cannot retroactively make inspected validation independent.

Inspect target-popularity buckets defined from training counts, cosine-residual/popularity correlation, and repeat-target versus unseen-target slices wherever permitted targets and histories support them. Keep these analyses separate from selection. Full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty real training users, five per category, cannot directly benefit from recommending consumed items. Their qualitative feedback does not establish benchmark gains or unobserved preferences. No executable replacement train.py is specified because the supplied input contains no baseline implementation or predictor interface.
idea.pseudocode:
Prespecify primary configurations, controls, checkpoint rule, numerical settings and complete search scope.
For each of the four categories:
  Train SASRec through the existing pipeline; record checkpoint selection; freeze parameters; enter eval mode.
  E[i] = normalize(item_embedding[i], eps=1e-8); E[0] = 0.
  Reconstruct fixed causal calibration pairs from training only with dedicated seed 42.
  For K in {3,10}:
    For each input position t:
      events = nonpadding inputs through t, including input[t], excluding target[t].
      r[t] = normalize(mean(E[last min(K,len(events)) events]), eps=1e-8).
      Use zero for an empty prefix; preserve repeated events.
    On identical valid calibration positions and negatives:
      db = base_score(t,positive) - base_score(t,negative).
      dc = dot(r[t],E[positive]) - dot(r[t],E[negative]).
    Compute float64 population standard deviations sb and sc over finite pairs.
    k = 0 if insufficient pairs, nonfinite scales, or sc <= 1e-3; else min(sb/sc,100).
    Record scales, margin means, correlation and sampling specification.
    score(t,i;alpha,K) = base_score(t,i) + alpha*k*dot(r[t],E[i]).
Compare baseline and six shared (K,alpha) configurations, alpha in {0.05,0.10,0.20}, on identical pinned validation users and candidates.
Select highest equally weighted four-category macro HR@10; prefer baseline on ties, then smaller alpha and K.
Run prespecified last-item, full-prefix, random-K, oldest-K and training-popularity controls with the same alpha grid and normalization protocol; disclose whether they are diagnostic only or included in selection before examining results.
Serialize all selected settings and write the matching predictor.
Verify exported/diagnostic score agreement, padding, repeated-event behavior, finite scores and future-token invariance.
Run residual-on/off diagnostics on identical training pairs; report corrected/regressed pairs separately from validation.
Report all configurations and paired category gains/losses; bootstrap users jointly across models within categories for descriptive macro intervals.
Inspect training-count popularity and repeat/unseen slices without treating them as evidence of unobserved user needs.

originality.positive: Combines frozen sequential scores with explicit margin-scale normalization, causal pooling and controlled residual ablations.
originality.negative: Recent-history pooling and additive similarity scoring are established techniques; controls improve credibility rather than algorithmic novelty.

future_potential.positive: Provides an inexpensive foundation for testing adaptive horizons and history-dependent residual strengths after establishing incremental signal.
future_potential.negative: Shared embeddings can produce redundant or popularity-driven gains, and cosine similarity cannot identify compatibility, fulfilled needs or whether another purchase is wanted.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no additional encoder training, external datasets or downloaded weights; scoring and most controls can reuse a frozen checkpoint.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal prefix alignment, repeated events, stable scale estimation, diagnostic compatibility, predictor equivalence and reproducible selection require more care than a simple score addition.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias
contributions: The supplied summary motivates measuring excessive emphasis on recent interactions.
limitations: Does not establish the useful residual strength or history horizon for this task.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains why sampled evaluation can disagree with full-catalog evaluation, including model-order reversals.
limitations: Does not determine which model improves the pinned benchmark; direct validation remains necessary.
Fixed candidates improve comparison consistency but do not establish full-catalog ranking gains.

related_work.title: LLM-enhanced complementary reranking paper
contributions: The supplied summary motivates distinguishing complementary relationships from broad similarity.
limitations: Textual relationship judgments do not verify compatibility or user needs.
Its LLM-based approach is not required for the selected embedding-only experiment.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains selection-induced optimism and motivates separating tuning from independent assessment.
limitations: Does not supply an independent assessment for already inspected benchmark validation results.

related_work.title: Original SASRec implementation
contributions: Provides causal attention, padding handling and final-position inference conventions relevant to the adapter.
limitations: The actual RecHarness baseline implementation remains authoritative; this reference cannot replace its interfaces or preprocessing.

related_work.title: RepeatNet: A Repeat Aware Neural Recommendation Machine for Session-based Recommendation
contributions: Motivates distinguishing repeat consumption from exploration.
limitations: Does not establish whether repeated events should receive greater weight in these datasets.
Unseen-item simulator recommendations cannot directly exploit repeat-item recommendations.

related_work.title: Google recommendation similarity guidance
contributions: Explains differences among embedding similarity measures and motivates considering embedding-norm effects.
limitations: Cosine normalization does not demonstrate the absence of popularity information in embedding directions.

related_work.title: NIST measures of scale
contributions: Describes scale estimators and robust alternatives relevant to heavy-tailed margin distributions.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed margin-ratio fusion rule, numerical thresholds or ranking benefits.
